const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/audit_artipacked.py
+"""Offline implementation of common actions/checkout credential findings."""
+import os
+import re
+
+from finding import finding, finding_location
+
+
+def audit_artipacked(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "Regular") -> list[dict]:
+    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
+    starts, offset = [], 0
+    for line in lines:
+        starts.append(offset)
+        offset += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
+    out = []
+    job = None
+    in_steps = False
+    step_idx = -1
+    step_indent = -1
+    i = 0
+    while i < len(lines):
+        raw = lines[i].rstrip("\r\n")
+        indent = len(raw) - len(raw.lstrip(" "))
+        stripped = raw.strip()
+        if indent == 0:
+            in_steps = False
+            job = None
+        if re.match(r"^jobs\s*:", raw):
+            job = None
+        elif re.match(r"^  [^\s#][^:]*:\s*(?:#.*)?$", raw):
+            job = raw.strip().split(":", 1)[0].strip("'\"")
+            in_steps = False
+        elif job is not None and re.match(r"^\s+steps\s*:", raw):
+            in_steps = True
+            step_idx = -1
+            step_indent = indent
+        elif in_steps and stripped.startswith("-"):
+            step_idx += 1
+        if in_steps and re.search(r"\buses\s*:\s*actions/checkout@", raw):
+            start_line = i
+            base_indent = indent
+            j = i + 1
+            false_set = False
+            while j < len(lines):
+                nextline = lines[j].rstrip("\r\n")
+                nstrip = nextline.strip()
+                nindent = len(nextline) - len(nextline.lstrip(" "))
+                if nstrip and nindent <= base_indent:
+                    break
+                if re.match(r"^\s+persist-credentials\s*:\s*false\s*(?:#.*)?$", nextline, re.I):
+                    false_set = True
+                j += 1
+            if not false_set:
+                # The analyzer highlights the `uses:` mapping, omitting the
+                # list marker and preserving the line ending in the feature.
+                body = lines[start_line].rstrip("\r\n")
+                key_col = body.find("uses:")
+                start = starts[start_line] + len(body[:key_col].encode("utf-8"))
+                end_line = j - 1
+                end = starts[end_line] + len(lines[end_line].encode("utf-8"))
+                route = ["jobs", job, "steps", step_idx]
+                loc = finding_location(filename, "does not set persist-credentials: false",
+                                       route, text, start, end)
+                ver = re.search(r"actions/checkout@([^\s#]+)", raw)
+                severity = "Low" if ver and re.match(r"v?6(?:\.|$)", ver.group(1), re.I) else "Medium"
+                out.append(finding("artipacked", "credential persistence through GitHub Actions artifacts",
+                                   severity, "Low", persona, [loc]))
+            i = j
+        else:
+            i += 1
+    return out
*** End Patch";

+"""Pedantic concurrency-limits checks for workflows."""
+import re
+
+from finding import finding, finding_location
+
+
+def audit_concurrency(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "regular") -> list[dict]:
+    if persona.lower() not in ("pedantic", "auditor"):
+        return []
+    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
+    offsets, pos = [], 0
+    for line in lines:
+        offsets.append(pos)
+        pos += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
+    if not any(re.match(r"^jobs\s*:", x) for x in lines):
+        return []
+    # A workflow level concurrency group provides the global limit.
+    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
+        if re.match(r"^concurrency\s*:", line):
+            return []
+    on_i = next((i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if re.match(r"^on\s*:", line)), None)
+    if on_i is None:
+        return []
+    on_line = lines[on_i].rstrip("\r\n")
+    start, end = offsets[on_i], offsets[on_i] + len(on_line.encode("utf-8"))
+    primary = finding_location(filename, "workflow is missing concurrency setting",
+                               ["on"], text, start, end)
+    locations = [primary]
+    jobs_i = next(i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if re.match(r"^jobs\s*:", line))
+    i = jobs_i + 1
+    while i < len(lines):
+        line = lines[i].rstrip("\r\n")
+        stripped = line.strip()
+        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip(" "))
+        if stripped and not stripped.startswith("#") and indent == 0:
+            break
+        m = re.match(r"^\s{2}([^#][^:]*?)\s*:\s*(?:#.*)?$", line)
+        if not m:
+            i += 1
+            continue
+        job = m.group(1).strip().strip("'\"")
+        job_indent = 2
+        j = i + 1
+        has_concurrency = False
+        while j < len(lines):
+            sub = lines[j].rstrip("\r\n")
+            sub_indent = len(sub) - len(sub.lstrip(" "))
+            if sub.strip() and not sub.lstrip().startswith("#") and sub_indent <= job_indent:
+                break
+            if re.match(r"^\s+concurrency\s*:", sub):
+                has_concurrency = True
+            j += 1
+        if not has_concurrency:
+            token = m.group(1).strip()
+            col = line.find(token)
+            if token.startswith(("'", '"')) and token[-1:] == token[:1]:
+                col += 1
+                token = token[1:-1]
+            offset = offsets[i] + len(line[:col].encode("utf-8"))
+            locations.append(finding_location(
+                filename, "job affected by missing workflow concurrency",
+                ["jobs", job], text, offset, offset + len(token.encode("utf-8")),
+                kind="Related", feature_kind="KeyOnly"))
+        i = j
+    if len(locations) == 1:
+        return []
+    return [finding("concurrency-limits", "insufficient job-level concurrency limits",
+                    "Low", "High", "Pedantic", locations)]
*** End Patch";

UNTRUSTED = re.compile(r"github\.event\.(?:issue\.(?:title|body)|pull_request\.(?:title|body)|comment\.(?:body)|review\.(?:body)|discussion\.(?:title|body))", re.I)
EXPR = re.compile(r"\$\{\{\s*(.*?)\s*\}\}")


def audit_template_injection(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "Regular") -> list[dict]:
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offsets, off = [], 0
    for line in lines:
        offsets.append(off); off += len(line)
    jobs = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        jm = re.match(r"^\s{2}([^\s#][^:]*):\s*(?:#.*)?$", line.rstrip("\r\n"))
        if jm:
            jobs.append((i, jm.group(1).strip().strip("'\"")))
    results = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        # run: and script-like code contexts are analyzed; inline expressions
        # in env/with values do not execute as code directly.
        key = re.match(r"^(\s*)(?:-\s*)?(run|script|inlineScript)\s*:\s*(.*?)(?:\r?\n)?$", line, re.I)
        if not key:
            continue
        indent = len(key.group(1))
        jobpair = next(((n, name) for n, name in reversed(jobs) if n < i), None)
        if not jobpair:
            continue
        job_i, job = jobpair
        step_i = next((k for k in range(i, job_i, -1) if re.match(r"^\s{6}-\s+", lines[k])), None)
        job_route = ["jobs", job]
        if step_i is not None:
            step_indent = len(lines[step_i]) - len(lines[step_i].lstrip())
            index = sum(1 for k in range(job_i + 1, step_i + 1)
                        if re.match(r"^\s{%d}-\s+" % step_indent, lines[k])) - 1
            route = job_route + ["steps", index]
        else:
            route = job_route
        code_start_line = i
        code_end_line = i + 1
        if key.group(3).strip() in ("|", ">", "|-", ">-") or not key.group(3).strip():
            while code_end_line < len(lines):
                s = lines[code_end_line].rstrip("\r\n")
                if s.strip() and len(s) - len(s.lstrip()) <= indent:
                    break
                code_end_line += 1
        code_start = offsets[code_start_line] + key.start(2)
        code_end = offsets[code_end_line] if code_end_line < len(lines) else len(text)
        # Find expressions in source lines inside the code field.
        matches = []
        for row in range(i, code_end_line):
            body = lines[row].rstrip("\r\n")
            for em in EXPR.finditer(body):
                expression = em.group(1)
                if UNTRUSTED.search(expression) or persona.lower() in ("pedantic", "auditor"):
                    matches.append((row, em, expression))
        if not matches:
            continue
        step_start_line = step_i if step_i is not None else i
        dash_match = re.match(r"^(\s*)-\s+", lines[step_start_line])
        related_start = offsets[step_start_line] + len(dash_match.group(1)) + 2 if dash_match else offsets[i] + lines[i].find(key.group(2) + ":")
        related_end_line = step_start_line + 1
        step_indent = len(dash_match.group(1)) if dash_match else indent
        while related_end_line < len(lines):
            body = lines[related_end_line].rstrip("\r\n")
            ind = len(body) - len(body.lstrip())
            if body.strip() and (ind <= step_indent or re.match(r"^\s{%d}-\s+" % step_indent, lines[related_end_line])):
                break
            related_end_line += 1
        related_end = offsets[related_end_line] if related_end_line < len(lines) else len(text)
        locations = []
        locations.append(finding_location(filename, "this step", route, text,
                                          related_start, related_end, kind="Hidden"))
        for row, em, expression in matches:
            # Source spans point at the expression body; the displayed feature
            # includes the surrounding command through the interpolation.
            mstart = offsets[row] + em.start(1)
            mend = offsets[row] + em.end(1)
            feature_start = offsets[i] + key.start(3)
            expr_route = route + ["run"]
            primary = finding_location(filename, "may expand into attacker-controllable code",
                expr_route, text, mstart, mend,
                feature_kind={"Subfeature": {"after": 6, "fragment": {"Raw": UNTRUSTED.search(expression).group(0) if UNTRUSTED.search(expression) else expression}}})
            primary["concrete"]["feature"] = text[feature_start:offsets[row] + em.end()]
            locations.append(primary)
            # Related key-only location indicates the run field containing code.
            key_start = offsets[i] + key.start(2)
            key_end = key_start + len(key.group(2))
            locations.append(finding_location(filename, f"this {key.group(2)} block", route + [key.group(2)],
                text, key_start, key_end, kind="Related", feature_kind="KeyOnly"))
        results.append(finding("template-injection", "code injection via template expansion",
                               "High", "High", persona, locations))
    return results

"""Offline implementation of common actions/checkout credential findings."""
import os
import re

from finding import finding, finding_location


def audit_artipacked(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "Regular") -> list[dict]:
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    starts, offset = [], 0
    for line in lines:
        starts.append(offset)
        offset += len(line)
    out = []
    job = None
    in_steps = False
    step_idx = -1
    step_indent = -1
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        raw = lines[i].rstrip("\r\n")
        indent = len(raw) - len(raw.lstrip(" "))
        stripped = raw.strip()
        if indent == 0:
            in_steps = False
            job = None
        if re.match(r"^jobs\s*:", raw):
            job = None
        elif re.match(r"^  [^\s#][^:]*:\s*(?:#.*)?$", raw):
            job = raw.strip().split(":", 1)[0].strip("'\"")
            in_steps = False
        elif job is not None and re.match(r"^\s+steps\s*:", raw):
            in_steps = True
            step_idx = -1
            step_indent = indent
        elif in_steps and stripped.startswith("-"):
            step_idx += 1
        if in_steps and re.search(r"\buses\s*:\s*actions/checkout@", raw):
            start_line = i
            base_indent = indent
            j = i + 1
            false_set = False
            while j < len(lines):
                nextline = lines[j].rstrip("\r\n")
                nstrip = nextline.strip()
                nindent = len(nextline) - len(nextline.lstrip(" "))
                if nstrip and nindent <= base_indent:
                    break
                if re.match(r"^\s+persist-credentials\s*:\s*false\s*(?:#.*)?$", nextline, re.I):
                    false_set = True
                j += 1
            if not false_set:
                # The analyzer highlights the `uses:` mapping, omitting the
                # list marker and preserving the line ending in the feature.
                body = lines[start_line].rstrip("\r\n")
                key_col = body.find("uses:")
                start = starts[start_line] + len(body[:key_col].encode("utf-8"))
                end_line = j - 1
                end = starts[end_line] + len(lines[end_line].rstrip("\r\n"))
                route = ["jobs", job, "steps", step_idx]
                loc = finding_location(filename, "does not set persist-credentials: false",
                                       route, text, start, end)
                ver = re.search(r"actions/checkout@([^\s#]+)", raw)
                severity = "Low" if ver and re.match(r"v?6(?:\.|$)", ver.group(1), re.I) else "Medium"
                out.append(finding("artipacked", "credential persistence through GitHub Actions artifacts",
                                   severity, "Low", persona, [loc]))
            i = j
        else:
            i += 1
    return out

"""Detect blanket secret inheritance by reusable workflows."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re

from finding import finding, finding_location


def audit_secrets_inherit(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "regular") -> list[dict]:
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offsets = []
    off = 0
    for line in lines:
        offsets.append(off)
        off += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
    path = os.path.abspath(filename)
    jobs = []
    job = None
    for i, raw in enumerate(lines):
        line = raw.rstrip("\r\n")
        if len(line) - len(line.lstrip()) == 2:
            m = re.match(r"^\s{2}([^:#]+)\s*:\s*$", line)
            if m:
                job = {"name": m.group(1).strip("'\""), "uses": None, "secrets": None}
                jobs.append(job)
        if job is None:
            continue
        use = re.match(r"^\s{4}uses\s*:\s*(.*?)\s*(?:#.*)?$", line)
        if use:
            v = use.group(1).strip().strip("'\"")
            col = line.find(":") + 1
            while col < len(line) and line[col].isspace():
                col += 1
            job["uses"] = (i, col, v)
        sec = re.match(r"^\s{4}secrets\s*:\s*(.*?)\s*(?:#.*)?$", line)
        if sec and sec.group(1).strip().strip("'\"") == "inherit":
            job["secrets"] = i

    out = []
    for job in jobs:
        if not job["uses"] or job["secrets"] is None:
            continue
        row, col, ref = job["uses"]
        sec_row = job["secrets"]
        use_start = offsets[row] + len(lines[row][:col].encode("utf-8"))
        use_end = use_start + len(ref.encode("utf-8"))
        sec_start = offsets[sec_row]
        sec_end = sec_start + len(lines[sec_row].rstrip("\r\n").encode("utf-8"))
        locations = [
            finding_location(path, "this reusable workflow", ["jobs", job["name"], "uses"], text, use_start, use_end,
                             feature_kind={"Subfeature": {"after": 0, "fragment": {"Raw": ref}}}),
            finding_location(path, "inherits all parent secrets", ["jobs", job["name"], "secrets"], text, sec_start, sec_end,
                             kind="Related"),
        ]
        out.append(finding("secrets-inherit", "secrets unconditionally inherited by called workflow", "Medium", "High", persona.capitalize(), locations))
    return out

"""Self-hosted runner audit (available in auditor persona)."""
import re
from finding import finding, finding_location


def audit_self_hosted_runner(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "Regular") -> list[dict]:
    if persona.lower() != "auditor":
        return []
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offsets, pos = [], 0
    for line in lines:
        offsets.append(pos); pos += len(line)
    jobs = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        m = re.match(r"^\s{2}([^\s#][^:]*):\s*(?:#.*)?$", line.rstrip("\r\n"))
        if m:
            jobs.append((i, m.group(1).strip().strip("'\"")))
    results = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        m = re.match(r"^(\s*)runs-on\s*:\s*(.*?)(?:\r?\n)?$", line, re.I)
        if not m or not re.search(r"(?:^|[\[ ,])self-hosted(?:$|[\], ])", m.group(2), re.I):
            continue
        parent = next(((j, name) for j, name in reversed(jobs) if j < i), None)
        if not parent:
            continue
        job_i, job = parent
        start = offsets[i] + len(m.group(1))
        end = offsets[i] + len(line.rstrip("\r\n"))
        loc = finding_location(filename, "self-hosted runner used here", ["jobs", job, "runs-on"],
                               text, start, end)
        loc["concrete"]["feature"] = line.rstrip("\r\n")
        results.append(finding("self-hosted-runner", "runs on a self-hosted runner", "Medium", "High",
                               persona.capitalize(), [loc]))
    return results

"""Detect attacker-controlled writes to GitHub Actions environment files."""
import re
from finding import finding, finding_location

UNTRUSTED = re.compile(r"github\.(?:event\.(?:issue|pull_request|comment|review|discussion)\.|head_ref)", re.I)


def audit_github_env(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "Regular") -> list[dict]:
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    starts = []
    pos = 0
    for line in lines:
        starts.append(pos)
        pos += len(line)
    # This audit is gated on triggers that run in the base repository context.
    on_value = "\n".join(line for line in lines if re.match(r"^(?:on\s*:|\s+(?:pull_request_target|workflow_run)\s*:)", line))
    if not re.search(r"\b(?:pull_request_target|workflow_run)\b", on_value):
        return []
    findings = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        m = re.match(r"^(\s*(?:-\s*)?)run\s*:", line)
        if not m:
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        j = i + 1
        while j < len(lines):
            candidate = lines[j]
            if candidate.strip() and not candidate.lstrip().startswith("#"):
                nindent = len(candidate) - len(candidate.lstrip())
                if nindent <= indent:
                    break
            j += 1
        block = "".join(lines[i:j])
        target = "GITHUB_ENV" if re.search(r"\$\{?GITHUB_ENV\}?", block) else "GITHUB_PATH" if re.search(r"\$\{?GITHUB_PATH\}?", block) else None
        if not target or not UNTRUSTED.search(block):
            continue
        job = None
        for k in range(i - 1, -1, -1):
            jm = re.match(r"^\s{2}([^\s#][^:]*):\s*(?:#.*)?(?:\r?\n)?$", lines[k])
            if jm and k > 0 and re.match(r"^jobs\s*:", lines[k - 1]):
                job = jm.group(1).strip(" '\"")
                break
        step_start = i
        for k in range(i, -1, -1):
            if re.match(r"^\s*-\s", lines[k]):
                step_start = k
                break
        list_indent = len(lines[step_start]) - len(lines[step_start].lstrip())
        step_index = sum(1 for k in range(step_start + 1, i + 1)
                         if re.match(r"^\s*-\s", lines[k]) and
                         len(lines[k]) - len(lines[k].lstrip()) == list_indent)
        route = ["jobs", job, "steps", step_index, "run"] if job is not None else ["runs", "steps", step_index, "run"]
        key_start = starts[i] + len(m.group(1))
        end = starts[j] if j < len(lines) else len(text)
        loc = finding_location(filename, f"write to {target} may allow code execution",
                               route, text, key_start, end)
        findings.append(finding("github-env", "dangerous use of environment file",
                                "High", "Low", persona, [loc]))
    return findings
"""Flag non-token secrets referenced by jobs without an environment."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re

from finding import finding, finding_location


_SECRET = re.compile(r"\$\{\{\s*secrets\.([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*\}\}")


def audit_secrets_outside_env(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "regular",
                              allow: set[str] | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    if persona.lower() != "auditor":
        return []
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offsets, offset = [], 0
    for line in lines:
        offsets.append(offset)
        offset += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
    starts = []
    for i, raw in enumerate(lines):
        m = re.match(r"^  ([^\s#][^:]*):\s*(?:#.*)?$", raw.rstrip("\r\n"))
        if m:
            starts.append((i, m.group(1).strip("'\"")))
    findings = []
    for index, (start_line, job) in enumerate(starts):
        end = offsets[starts[index+1][0]] if index + 1 < len(starts) else len(text.encode("utf-8"))
        start = offsets[start_line]
        block = text.encode("utf-8")[start:end].decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        if re.search(r"(?m)^\s{4}environment\s*:", block):
            continue
        key_col = lines[start_line].find(job)
        name_start = offsets[start_line] + key_col
        name_end = name_start + len(job.encode("utf-8"))
        related = finding_location(os.path.abspath(filename), "this job", ["jobs", job], text,
                                   name_start, name_end, kind="Related", feature_kind="KeyOnly")
        for match in _SECRET.finditer(block):
            secret = match.group(1)
            if secret == "GITHUB_TOKEN" or (allow and secret in allow):
                continue
            before = block[:match.start(1)]
            primary_start = start + len(before.encode("utf-8"))
            # Locate the full context name; the source span intentionally
            # excludes the surrounding `${{ ... }}` delimiters.
            primary_end = primary_start + len(("secrets." + secret).encode("utf-8"))
            primary = finding_location(os.path.abspath(filename), "secret is accessed outside of a dedicated environment",
                                       ["jobs", job], text, primary_start, primary_end)
            findings.append(finding("secrets-outside-env", "secrets referenced without a dedicated environment",
                                    "Medium", "High", "Auditor", [related, primary]))
    return findings

## `template-injection`

| Type     | Examples                 | Introduced in | Works offline  | Auto-fixes available | Configurable |
|----------|--------------------------|---------------|----------------|--------------------| ---------------|
| Workflow, Action  | [template-injection.yml] | v0.1.0        | ✅             | ✅        | ❌  |

[template-injection.yml]: https://github.com/woodruffw/gha-hazmat/blob/main/.github/workflows/template-injection.yml

Detects potential sources of code injection via template expansion.

GitHub Actions allows workflows to define *template expansions*, which
occur within special `${{ ... }}` delimiters. These expansions happen
before workflow and job execution, meaning the expansion
of a given expression appears verbatim in whatever context it was performed in.

Template expansions aren't syntax-aware, meaning that they can result in
unintended shell injection vectors. This is especially true when they're
used with attacker-controllable expression contexts, such as
`github.event.issue.title` (which the attacker can fully control by supplying
a new issue title).

!!! tip

    When used with a "pedantic" or "auditor"
    [persona](./usage.md#using-personas), this audit will flag *all* template
    expansions in code contexts, even ones that are likely safe.

    This is because `zizmor` considers all template expansions in code contexts
    to be code smells, and attempting to selectively permit them is more
    error-prone than forbidding them in a blanket fashion.

Other resources:

* [Keeping your GitHub Actions and workflows secure Part 2: Untrusted input]

### Remediation

The most common forms of template injection are in `run:` and similar
code-execution blocks. In these cases, an inline template expansion
can typically be replaced by an environment variable whose value comes
from the expanded template.

This avoids the vulnerability, since variable expansion is subject to normal
shell quoting/expansion rules.

!!! tip

    To fully remediate the vulnerability, you **should not** use
    `${{ env.VARNAME }}`, since that is still a template expansion.
    Instead, you should use `${VARNAME}` to ensure that the shell *itself*
    performs the variable expansion.


!!! tip

    When switching to `${VARNAME}`, keep in mind that different shells have
    different environment variable syntaxes. In particular, Powershell (the
    default shell on Windows runners) uses `${env:VARNAME}`.

    To avoid having to specialize your handling for different runners,
    you can set `#!yaml shell: sh` or `#!yaml shell: bash`.

!!! example

    === "Before :warning:"

        ```yaml title="template-injection.yml" hl_lines="3"
        - name: Check title
          run: |
            title="${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
            if [[ ! $title =~ ^.*:\ .*$ ]]; then
              echo "Bad issue title"
              exit 1
            fi
        ```

def format_plain(findings: list[dict], sources: dict[str, str], *, show_urls: bool = True) -> str:
    """Render compact cargo-style diagnostics for plain output."""
    if not findings:
        return "No findings to report. Good job!\n"
    lines_out: list[str] = []
    for item in findings:
        ident, desc = item.get("ident", ""), item.get("desc", "")
        det = item.get("determinations", {})
        severity = str(det.get("severity", "Medium"))
        level = {"High": "error", "Medium": "warning", "Low": "help",
                 "Informational": "info"}.get(severity, "warning")
        lines_out.append(f"{level}[{ident}]: {desc}")
        locations = item.get("locations", [])
        for idx, loc in enumerate(locations):
            sym = loc.get("symbolic", {})
            concrete = loc.get("concrete", {})
            key = sym.get("key", {})
            local = key.get("Local", {})
            path = local.get("given_path", "<stdin>" if "Stdin" in key else "")
            point = concrete.get("location", {})
            start, end = point.get("start_point", {}), point.get("end_point", {})
            row, col = start.get("row", 0), start.get("column", 0)
            feature = concrete.get("feature", "")
            source = sources.get(path, "")
            source_lines = source.splitlines()
            end_row, end_col = end.get("row", row), end.get("column", col + 1)
            if end_col == 0 and end_row > row:
                end_row -= 1
                end_col = len(source_lines[end_row]) if end_row < len(source_lines) else 0
            lines_out.append(f" --> {path}:{row + 1}:{col + 1}")
            lines_out.append("  |")
            if source_lines and row < len(source_lines):
                first_row = row
                last_row = min(end_row, len(source_lines) - 1)
                width = len(str(last_row + 1))
                for line_no in range(first_row, last_row + 1):
                    source_line = source_lines[line_no]
                    lines_out.append(f"{line_no + 1:>{width}} | {source_line}")
                    if line_no == first_row and line_no == last_row:
                        length = max(1, end_col - col)
                        marker = " " * col + "^" * length
                        annotation = sym.get("annotation", "")
                        lines_out.append(f"{'':>{width}} | {marker} {annotation}".rstrip())
            elif feature:
                lines_out.append(f"{row + 1} | {feature.rstrip()}")
                lines_out.append(f"  | {' ' * col}^{' ' + sym.get('annotation', '')}")
            lines_out.append("  |")
        lines_out.append(f"  = note: audit confidence → {det.get('confidence', 'High')}")
        if ident in ("artipacked", "template-injection", "dangerous-triggers"):
            lines_out.append("  = note: this finding has an auto-fix")
        if show_urls:
            lines_out.append(f"  = help: audit documentation → {item.get('url', '')}")
        lines_out.append("")
    counts = {k: sum(str(f.get("determinations", {}).get("severity", "")).lower() == k
                     for f in findings) for k in ("informational", "low", "medium", "high")}
    lines_out.append(f"{len(findings)} findings: {counts['informational']} informational, "
                     f"{counts['low']} low, {counts['medium']} medium, {counts['high']} high")
    return "\n".join(lines_out) + "\n"

"""Offline implementation of common actions/checkout credential findings."""
import os
import re

from finding import finding, finding_location


def audit_artipacked(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "Regular") -> list[dict]:
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    starts, offset = [], 0
    for line in lines:
        starts.append(offset)
        offset += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
    out = []
    job = None
    in_steps = False
    step_idx = -1
    step_indent = -1
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        raw = lines[i].rstrip("\r\n")
        indent = len(raw) - len(raw.lstrip(" "))
        stripped = raw.strip()
        if indent == 0:
            in_steps = False
            job = None
        if re.match(r"^jobs\s*:", raw):
            job = None
        elif re.match(r"^  [^\s#][^:]*:\s*(?:#.*)?$", raw):
            job = raw.strip().split(":", 1)[0].strip("'\"")
            in_steps = False
        elif job is not None and re.match(r"^\s+steps\s*:", raw):
            in_steps = True
            step_idx = -1
            step_indent = indent
        elif in_steps and stripped.startswith("-"):
            step_idx += 1
        if in_steps and re.search(r"\buses\s*:\s*actions/checkout@", raw):
            start_line = i
            base_indent = indent
            j = i + 1
            false_set = False
            while j < len(lines):
                nextline = lines[j].rstrip("\r\n")
                nstrip = nextline.strip()
                nindent = len(nextline) - len(nextline.lstrip(" "))
                if nstrip and nindent <= base_indent:
                    break
                if re.match(r"^\s+persist-credentials\s*:\s*false\s*(?:#.*)?$", nextline, re.I):
                    false_set = True
                j += 1
            if not false_set:
                # The analyzer highlights the `uses:` mapping, omitting the
                # list marker and preserving the line ending in the feature.
                body = lines[start_line].rstrip("\r\n")
                key_col = body.find("uses:")
                start = starts[start_line] + len(body[:key_col].encode("utf-8"))
                end_line = j - 1
                # A final source node owns its terminal newline; an interior
                # YAML node stops before the sibling separator newline.
                end_text = (lines[end_line] if end_line == len(lines) - 1
                            else lines[end_line].rstrip("\r\n"))
                end = starts[end_line] + len(end_text.encode("utf-8"))
                route = ["jobs", job, "steps", step_idx]
                loc = finding_location(filename, "does not set persist-credentials: false",
                                       route, text, start, end)
                ver = re.search(r"actions/checkout@([^\s#]+)", raw)
                severity = "Low" if ver and re.match(r"v?6(?:\.|$)", ver.group(1), re.I) else "Medium"
                out.append(finding("artipacked", "credential persistence through GitHub Actions artifacts",
                                   severity, "Low", persona, [loc]))
            i = j
        else:
            i += 1
    return out

"""Offline unpinned container image audit."""
import re
from finding import finding, finding_location

SHA256 = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$")


def audit_unpinned_images(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "Regular") -> list[dict]:
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    result = []
    stack = []  # (indent, mapping key)
    offset = 0
    for line in lines:
        raw = line.rstrip("\r\n")
        m = re.match(r"^(\s*)(?:-\s*)?([^:#][^:]*?)\s*:\s*(.*?)\s*$", raw)
        if not m:
            offset += len(line)
            continue
        indent = len(m.group(1))
        key = m.group(2).strip().strip("'\"")
        value = m.group(3).split(" #", 1)[0].strip().strip("'\"")
        while stack and stack[-1][0] >= indent:
            stack.pop()
        ancestors = [x[1] for x in stack]
        if key == "image" and "jobs" in ancestors and ("container" in ancestors or "services" in ancestors):
            job_i = ancestors.index("jobs") + 1
            if job_i < len(ancestors):
                job = ancestors[job_i]
                # SHA256 digests are immutable; tags other than `latest` are
                # emitted only in the pedantic/auditor persona.
                if "@" in value:
                    digest = value.rsplit("@sha256:", 1)[1] if "@sha256:" in value else ""
                    pinned = bool(SHA256.fullmatch(digest))
                    latest = False
                else:
                    last = value.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
                    has_tag = ":" in last
                    tag = last.rsplit(":", 1)[1] if has_tag else ""
                    pinned = has_tag and tag.lower() != "latest"
                    latest = has_tag and tag.lower() == "latest"
                pedantic = persona.lower() in ("pedantic", "auditor")
                emit = latest or not pinned or (pedantic and pinned)
                if emit:
                    annotation = ("container image is pinned to latest" if latest else
                                  "container image is not pinned to a SHA256 hash" if pedantic and pinned else
                                  "container image is unpinned")
                    route = ["jobs", job] + ancestors[job_i + 1:] + ["image"]
                    start = offset + len(m.group(1))
                    end = offset + len(raw)
                    loc = finding_location(filename, annotation, route, text,
                                           start, end)
                    # Concrete feature projection includes source indentation,
                    # while the highlighted span begins at the YAML key.
                    loc["concrete"]["feature"] = raw
                    result.append(finding("unpinned-images", "unpinned image references",
                                          "High", "High", persona, [loc]))
        # A mapping node with children stays on the stack. Scalar mappings are
        # also harmless ancestors for the subsequent sibling-pop logic.
        stack.append((indent, key))
        offset += len(line)
    return result

"""Detect action inputs that implicitly select the latest external tool."""
import re
from finding import finding, finding_location


def audit_unpinned_tools(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "Regular") -> list[dict]:
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    starts = []
    pos = 0
    for line in lines:
        starts.append(pos)
        pos += len(line)
    jobs = None
    job = None
    steps_indent = None
    step_index = -1
    entries = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        raw = line.rstrip("\r\n")
        indent = len(raw) - len(raw.lstrip())
        stripped = raw.strip()
        if indent == 0:
            jobs = stripped == "jobs:"
            job = None
            steps_indent = None
        elif jobs and indent == 2 and stripped.endswith(":"):
            job = stripped[:-1].strip(" '\"")
            steps_indent = None
        elif job is not None and stripped == "steps:":
            steps_indent = indent
            step_index = -1
        if steps_indent is None or not stripped:
            continue
        if indent > steps_indent and stripped.startswith("-"):
            step_index += 1
        m = re.match(r"^\s*-\s*uses\s*:\s*(.*?)\s*(?:#.*)?$", raw)
        if not m:
            continue
        value = m.group(1).strip().strip("'\"")
        if not value.lower().startswith("1password/load-secrets-action@"):
            continue
        # Inputs belong to this step until its next list item or a peer property.
        j = i + 1
        with_indent = None
        version_line = None
        version_value = None
        while j < len(lines):
            r = lines[j].rstrip("\r\n")
            s = r.strip()
            ind = len(r) - len(r.lstrip())
            if s and ind <= indent:
                break
            if re.match(r"^\s+with\s*:", r):
                with_indent = ind
            elif with_indent is not None and ind > with_indent:
                vm = re.match(r"^\s*version\s*:\s*(.*?)\s*(?:#.*)?$", r)
                if vm:
                    version_line = j
                    version_value = vm.group(1).strip().strip("'\"")
            j += 1
        if version_value and version_value.lower() != "latest":
            continue
        uses_offset = starts[i] + raw.find(value)
        uses_end = uses_offset + len(value)
        route = ["jobs", job, "steps", step_index]
        locs = []
        base = finding_location(filename,
                                "action implicitly uses an unpinned latest version" if version_line is None else "this action",
                                route + ["uses"], text, uses_offset, uses_end,
                                kind="Primary" if version_line is None else "Related",
                                feature_kind={"Subfeature": {"after": 0, "fragment": {"Raw": value}}})
        locs.append(base)
        if version_line is not None:
            vr = lines[version_line].rstrip("\r\n")
            vstart = starts[version_line] + len(vr) - len(vr.lstrip())
            vloc = finding_location(filename, "specifies `version: latest` which is unpinned",
                                    route + ["with", "version"], text, vstart,
                                    starts[version_line] + len(vr))
            vloc["concrete"]["feature"] = vr
            locs.append(vloc)
        findings = finding("unpinned-tools", "action installs an unpinned external tool",
                           "Medium", "High", persona, locs)
        entries.append(findings)
    return entries

"""A lightweight offline implementation of the excessive-permissions audit."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from finding import finding, finding_location


def audit_excessive_permissions_workflow(text: str, filename: str,
                                        persona: str = "Pedantic") -> list[dict]:
    """Pedantic whole-workflow warning for inherited broad defaults."""
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offset = 0
    for i, raw in enumerate(lines):
        line = raw.rstrip("\r\n")
        m = re.match(r"^permissions\s*:\s*(read-all|write-all)\s*(?:#.*)?$", line)
        if m:
            level = m.group(1)
            end = offset + len(line)
            loc = finding_location(filename, f"uses {level} permissions", ["permissions"],
                                   text, offset, end)
            return [finding("excessive-permissions", "overly broad permissions",
                            "High" if level == "write-all" else "Medium", "High",
                            persona, [loc])]
        offset += len(raw)
    if any(re.match(r"^permissions\s*:", line.rstrip("\r\n")) for line in lines):
        return []
    if not any(re.match(r"^jobs\s*:", line) for line in lines):
        return []
    loc = finding_location(filename,
                           "default permissions used due to no permissions: block",
                           [], text, 0, len(text))
    return [finding("excessive-permissions", "overly broad permissions", "Medium",
                    "Medium", persona, [loc])]


def audit_read_all_permissions(text: str, filename: str,
                              persona: str = "Pedantic") -> list[dict]:
    """Pedantic finding for an explicitly broad workflow permission grant."""
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offset = 0
    for row, raw in enumerate(lines):
        line = raw.rstrip("\r\n")
        m = re.match(r"^permissions\s*:\s*(read-all|write-all)\s*(?:#.*)?$", line, re.I)
        if m:
            end = offset + len(line.encode("utf-8"))
            loc = finding_location(filename, f"uses {m.group(1).lower()} permissions",
                                   ["permissions"], text, offset, end)
            return [finding("excessive-permissions", "overly broad permissions", "Medium",
                            "High", persona, [loc])]
        offset += len(raw.encode("utf-8"))
    return []


def audit_excessive_permissions(text: str, filename: str,
                               persona: str = "Regular") -> list[dict]:
    """Report jobs which inherit GitHub's broad default token permissions.

    This intentionally operates on source indentation so emitted spans point
    back to the original YAML, without requiring a non-standard YAML package.
    """
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offsets = []
    at = 0
    for line in lines:
        offsets.append(at)
        at += len(line)

    # Locate top-level `permissions:`. A key at the top level applies to all
    # jobs; per-job permission keys suppress findings for that job only.
    workflow_permissions = any(
        re.match(r"^permissions\s*:", line.rstrip("\r\n")) for line in lines
    )
    jobs_idx = next((i for i, line in enumerate(lines)
                     if re.match(r"^jobs\s*:", line.rstrip("\r\n"))), None)
    if workflow_permissions or jobs_idx is None:
        return []

    jobs_indent = len(lines[jobs_idx]) - len(lines[jobs_idx].lstrip(" "))
    found = []
    i = jobs_idx + 1
    while i < len(lines):
        raw = lines[i].rstrip("\r\n")
        stripped = raw.lstrip(" ")
        indent = len(raw) - len(stripped)
        if stripped and not stripped.startswith("#") and indent <= jobs_indent:
            break
        # Job IDs are immediate children of jobs. Permit quoted ids.
        m = re.match(r"^\s+([^#][^:]*):(?:\s*(?:#.*)?)?$", raw)
        if m and indent > jobs_indent:
            job_indent = indent
            start_line = i
            j = i + 1
            has_permissions = False
            while j < len(lines):
                r = lines[j].rstrip("\r\n")
                s = r.lstrip(" ")
                ind = len(r) - len(s)
                if s and not s.startswith("#") and ind <= job_indent:
                    break
                if re.match(r"^\s+permissions\s*:", r):
                    has_permissions = True
                j += 1
            if not has_permissions:
                # Match the job subtree, including its final line ending when
                # present; this is the span used by the reference diagnostic.
                end = offsets[j] if j < len(lines) else len(text)
                start = offsets[start_line]
                route = ["jobs", m.group(1).strip().strip("'\"")]
                loc_related = finding_location(
                    filename, "this job", route, text, start, end,
                    kind="Related")
                loc_primary = finding_location(
                    filename, "default permissions used due to no permissions: block",
                    route, text, start, end)

"""A lightweight offline implementation of the excessive-permissions audit."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from finding import finding, finding_location


def audit_excessive_permissions_workflow(text: str, filename: str,
                                        persona: str = "Pedantic") -> list[dict]:
    """Pedantic whole-workflow warning for inherited broad defaults."""
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offset = 0
    for i, raw in enumerate(lines):
        line = raw.rstrip("\r\n")
        m = re.match(r"^permissions\s*:\s*(read-all|write-all)\s*(?:#.*)?$", line)
        if m:
            level = m.group(1)
            end = offset + len(line)
            loc = finding_location(filename, f"uses {level} permissions", ["permissions"],
                                   text, offset, end)
            return [finding("excessive-permissions", "overly broad permissions",
                            "High" if level == "write-all" else "Medium", "High",
                            persona, [loc])]
        offset += len(raw)
    if any(re.match(r"^permissions\s*:", line.rstrip("\r\n")) for line in lines):
        return []
    if not any(re.match(r"^jobs\s*:", line) for line in lines):
        return []
    loc = finding_location(filename,
                           "default permissions used due to no permissions: block",
                           [], text, 0, len(text))
    return [finding("excessive-permissions", "overly broad permissions", "Medium",
                    "Medium", persona, [loc])]


def audit_read_all_permissions(text: str, filename: str,
                              persona: str = "Pedantic") -> list[dict]:
    """Pedantic finding for an explicitly broad workflow permission grant."""
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offset = 0
    for row, raw in enumerate(lines):

        m = re.match(r"^permissions\s*:\s*(read-all|write-all)\s*(?:#.*)?$", line, re.I)
